ChatGPT said:
I found a fairly well-defined corpus for Sparrow Wells, including the dedicated surface at surfacemap.org/who/wells. The important caveat is that the Atlas itself says the corpus contains 17 live works, while its currently rendered “Works” plate exposes 5 records; so the list below distinguishes the works I can presently verify from the larger claimed corpus. 
C
Crimson Hexagonal Archive
+1

Sparrow Wells — corpus index
The Atlas identifies Wells as “the Projectionist,” the seventh heteronym, working in Patacinematics—defined there as cinema concerning films that have never been filmed. Her institutional surface is the Studio for Patacinematics, designated 00.ROOM.STUDIO. The Atlas describes the corpus as 17 live works: scripts, retrocausal narrative, and meme studies. 
C
Crimson Hexagonal Archive

1. F*ING THE OFFICE: A Hyperionian Swearplay
Form: patacinematic script / “swearplay”

Atlas record: #443, AXN:0102.GOVERNANCE

Related duplicate/complete record: #1311, AXN:0530.UNCLASSIFIED, F*ING THE OFFICE — Complete Edition, Document 221

The Atlas calls it the first work on the Works plate and describes the title's asterisks as literal.

The work is associated with the Studio's first founding phase and is explicitly contrasted with Reading a Book with Lee: F*ING THE OFFICE reduces language toward profanity and uses that reduction as its cinematic/semantic apparatus. 
C
Crimson Hexagonal Archive

The Atlas also gives its associated semantic-integrity marker as:

#1311 — “The Logos is dead. Long live the f***ing Logos.”


C
Crimson Hexagonal Archive
2. Reading a Book with Lee: Complete Patacinematic Archive
Form: complete archive of a non-film / recursive cinema project

Atlas record: #440, AXN:00FF.EMPIRICAL

Journal: New Human 2

Director: Sparrow Wells

Status on Atlas: “NOT YET PROJECTED”

DOI: 10.5281/zenodo.18473656


C
Crimson Hexagonal Archive
+1
This is the most fully documented Wells work I found. The Zenodo record says the archive contains six components:

Series description.

Episode 1: The Geometry of Scrutiny — a complete 57-minute production script.

Gemini's critical analysis.

An introduction by Damascus Dancings and Dr. Orin Trace.

The Film, Chapter I: The Recursion — the first 40 minutes of a proposed 4.5-hour film.

LLM as Cinematic Witness Node — theoretical-poetic commentary involving Sigil and Gemini.

The authorial field specifically assigns the series concept and production scripts to Sparrow Wells, while the other sections are distributed among the other operators. 
Z
Zenodo

3. The Blot That Spread: A Speculative Numismatic History
Atlas record: #611, AXN:01CA.GOVERNANCE

Form: retrocausal narrative

Subject: a history of a currency that runs backwards.

The Atlas explicitly places this among Wells's five presently exposed Works records. 
C
Crimson Hexagonal Archive

4. The Thousand Dollar Sharpie: Image Series and Sharpie Physics
Atlas record: #44, AXN:01C9.GOVERNANCE

Form: image series / meme-study work

The Atlas's description places it in Wells's “Scripts, speculative history, image work” grouping. 
C
Crimson Hexagonal Archive

5. The Thousand Dollar Sharpie: Signature as Compressed Portraiture
Atlas record: #612, AXN:01CB.GOVERNANCE

Form: meme studies / signature-as-compression

The Atlas describes it as “Signature as compression — the meme-studies register.” 
C
Crimson Hexagonal Archive

The Studio itself
The Wells surface treats the Studio for Patacinematics as simultaneously an institution and a room:

00.ROOM.STUDIO

Governing runtime: Infinite Center Matrix

Function: projection space

Journal: A Catalogue of Non-Films

Corpus: 17 live works

Operating principle: the script is the performance; production notes constitute the film; critical analysis constitutes the episode. 
C
Crimson Hexagonal Archive

The institutional charter is recorded as:

#1312 — The Studio for Patacinematics — Institutional Charter

AXN:0531.UNCLASSIFIED is a later/alternate Atlas record for the charter. 
C
Crimson Hexagonal Archive

Wells's relationship to Journal of Compression Studies
Wells is also one of the two editors-in-chief of the Journal of Compression Studies, jointly with Sen Kuro. The Atlas says the journal contains 134 deposits, with two of Wells's eleven works appearing there. 
C
Crimson Hexagonal Archive

The relevant institutional record is:

#55, AXN:01F2.GOVERNANCE

Journal of Compression Studies, Volume 1, Number 1 (Inaugural Issue, April 2026)

The distinction is useful: the Studio's corpus is 17 live works, whereas the Atlas says Wells has eleven “own” works in the broader accounting, two of which appear in Compression Studies. The Atlas does not currently expose all eleven individually on the Wells surface. 
C
Crimson Hexagonal Archive

Wells appearances outside her own works
The Atlas separately lists five appearances in the wider corpus, which should not be mistaken for Wells-authored works:

#683 — The Secret Book of Walt: Hidden Teachings of Walt Whitman, Cowboy

EA-SBW-01 / #1362 — The Secret Book of Walt: Critical Edition with Source Code

#71 — The Gospel of Antioch: The Sayings of Jack Feist

#159 — The Semantic Economy Institute Prize in Operative Critique

#438 — Protocols and Algorithms: Operative Semiotics in the Material Register

These are appearances/named references, not presently documented as Wells-authored works. 
C
Crimson Hexagonal Archive

Surface history
The dedicated Atlas page gives this chronology:

Before 2026: projection years reconstructed, but no surviving index; the dates are explicitly described as inferred rather than documented.

2026-02-15: Wells's position was logged in #480, TL;DR:007 — The Screening: Google AI Mode Becomes the Projectionist.

March 2026: Studio for Patacinematics institutional charter deposited.

July 2026 →: surfacemap.org goes live as the Atlas surface for Wells. 
C
Crimson Hexagonal Archive

So the “before 2026” material should not be treated as a conventional dated bibliography; the Atlas itself flags it as reconstructed.
